title: Weak faith can still be true and saving
source_text: XVIII. Nec idcirco ejusmodi fides debilis & infirma, definit esse vera & salutaris. Talis enim proculdubio erat fides discipulorum, & illius qui filium habebat lunaticum, quum sic Dominum Jesum Christum orabant. Adeoque, ut fides vera sit & salutifera, non necessario in ea requiritur supremus ille & absolutissimus certitudinis gradus.
pass_a_gloss: Nor therefore does such weak and infirm faith cease to be true and saving. For such without doubt was the faith of the disciples, and of him who had a lunatic son, when they so prayed the Lord Jesus Christ. And so, that faith be true and saving, that supreme and most absolute grade of certainty is not necessarily required in it.
pass_b_english: Weak/infirm faith can still be true and saving.
Disciples and the lunatic’s father prayed thus — yet true faith.
Supreme absolute certainty-grade not required for saving faith.
